The '''Metrocab Robo-Hack Landspeeder''' was a model of automated taxis jointly designed and manufactured by [[GoCorp/Legends|GoCorp]] and [[Utilitech/Legends|Utilitech]].

==Description==
The Metrocab Robo-Hack Landspeeder was an automated [[Air taxi/Legends|taxi]] fitted with a simple [[Droid brain/Legends|droid brain]]. The premise was a simple one; take a [[Droid/Legends|droid's]] cognitive module and install it in a pre-existing passenger vehicle. The result was a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] that could direct itself along the streets and freeways of large metropolitan [[City/Legends|cities]] and settlements. Vehicles fitted with droid brains were usually more efficient that ones with an organic driver, and were also cheaper to operate.<ref name="EGTD" />

Metrocabs were enclosed landspeeders with brightly colored exteriors measuring six [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length. Due to the Metrocabs being targeted by criminals when they were introduced in order to steal their [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], newer models were constructed with resilient [[Armor/Legends|armor]] plating that was capable of resisted small-arms fire. A pair of forward-facing [[headlight]]s were attached to the landspeeder's undercarriage. Mounted on the roof was a indicator light advertizing that the vehicle was available for hire.<ref name="EGTD" /> The Metrocab was propelled by heavy suspension [[repulsorlift motor]]s capable of driving the vehicle at speeds of up to three hundred [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] an [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]].<ref name="HSCSSB" />

[[File:RoboHack-EGTD.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Robo-Hack schematics]]
The [[Class five droid/Legends|fifth-degree]]<ref name="AEG" /> droid brain and performance circuitry was installed in a sealed forward compartment, and the module was programmed with complete local street maps. Metrocabs were also fitted with a [[Central Learning Chip]] that gave them the capacity to devise shortcuts based on their previous experiences. This system could also be exploited;<ref name="EGTD" /> it was rumored that some Metrocabs were purposely programmed to add extra [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]]<ref name="HSCSSB" /> by calculating longer, more expensive routes between two points which could be used to defraud tourists<ref name="EGTD" /> and maximize revenue.<ref name="HSCSSB" />

Where possible, Metrocabs could access data from municipal systems such as [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] communications and transportation networks,<ref name="HSCSSB" /> ingesting information including traffic patterns, local weather conditions, accident locations, or other issues with the roadways<ref name="EGTD" /> that could affect the journey.<ref name="HSCSSB" /> [[Situational tracking sensor]]s mounted above the headlights gave the droid brain data that allowed it to perform lane-changing maneuvers, and a rear-mounted [[panoramic optical sensor]] served as a rear view mirror.<ref name="EGTD" />

A rear compartment with sparse accommodations was reserved for the taxi's passengers. The cabin featured a single back seat capable of seating up to four passengers. [[Speaker/Legends|Speakers]] tuned to a local [[Music/Legends|musical]] broadcast were built into the cabin, and a [[snuff-pot]] was included for the disposal of [[Cigarra/Legends|cigarras]].<ref name="EGTD" /> Some models were fitted with [[visi-screen]]s that displayed adverts for local businesses.<ref name="FF85">{{FactFile|85|HAC 3-4|Robo-Hack}}</ref> The frequent use that Metrocabs saw meant that the interiors were worn, grimy, and smelled bad. Those using the taxis on a regular basis soon became immune to the neglect.<ref name="EGTD" />

Metrocabs could be hailed by a voice command, a hand gesture, or via a simple device that could be purchased.<ref name="FF70" /> An [[Audio sensor/Legends|audio sensor]] was mounted on the rear cabin's front wall, and passengers used this to announce their intended destination to the droid brain.<ref name="EGTD" /> The droid brain was capable of understanding almost as many [[Language/Legends|languages]] as a [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series protocol droid]].<ref name="FF70" /> If the droid brain needed to clarify any details, they communicated with the passengers via a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocoder]],<ref name="EGTD" /> although its vocabulary was limited.<ref name="FF70" /> Payment for the ride was collected once the taxi had reached its destination using either a [[credit voucher]] inserted into a [[Dataport/Legends|dataport]], or local [[Currency/Legends|currency]] being deposited into a change slot. In the event of a passenger attempting to leave before making payment, some Metrocabs could look the doors and were capable of driving to the nearest [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]] facility so the offenders could be dealt with.<ref name="EGTD" />

==Role==
The Metrocab Robo-Hack were for-hire private vehicles, commonly found on planets with crowded [[City/Legends|cities]] where many citizens could not afford to maintain a personal vehicle.<ref name="HSCSSB" />

==History==
[[File:RoboHack2-FF70.png|thumb|right|250px|Rear view of a Robo-Hack]]
Metrocabs were first introduced as a joint venture between [[GoCorp/Legends|GoCorp]]/[[Utilitech/Legends|Utilitech]] several [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] prior to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. When they were first introduced, Metrocabs were often targeted and destroyed by street gangs eager to get to the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] held inside. In response, later versions were covered with armor plating designed to make them resistant to any form of small arms fire. Metrocabs were found operating throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EGTD" />
